reviews.review:
TLDR: YES!

I don't normally buy games on a whim. It's not my style, but as an Indie developer myself, what I enjoy doing is browsing new releases to see what sticks out. What games do I click on, and why? Its an effective way to take information back to your own projects. 

When I saw this game, I clicked. And it took about a minute of the steam page before I bought it, and played through what I think is most of the main story, in one sitting. There's a chance I'm missing some main stuff, and defintely not all of the endings. I know how crucial reviews are to new releases, and so here I am. 

Let me preface my review by adding on that I am not a Visual Novel player. This will have been the first that could be described as such, and I'm probably not the target audience. However, I still enjoyed it, and have some feedback.
---
The biggest draw to this game is the absolutely incredible art style. It's this peculiar collection of neon colors amid a super-dark backdrop that i personally have always been drawn to, and its part of the reason why I bought this game. In that department, I have no notes. It is phenomenal, and I cant wait to see more. The story as well, intrigued me and kept me engaged throughout. I was invested well enough, even when some things cut off the suspension of disbelief (discussed later) and I had to get back into the headspace of the game. All in all, it was pretty good. The puzzles I found particularly enjoyable, even if the actions themselves weren't all that interesting. The soundtrack, when it comes in, is always a delight.

There are only a few things I didn't totally love, most are just nitpicks. The first is the controls, mainly how all movement is locked to tiles, preventing diagonal movement and making it feel slightly janky. If I'm remembering right, this is an engine limitation, and thats okay. It can be overlooked. Second, and do recall I do not know Visual Novels as well as probably the more intended audience, but I found some interactions and dialogue dragging, as a way to fill out the game a bit more, in terms of getting points and the story across. That might be perfectly acceptable for VNs and I just don't know. I play a lot of story based games, and am used to story being fed a bit slower, through slightly faster-paced interactions and player deduction. Whereas this defintely feels like closer to watching a slow-paced movie, which some will totally love, and I got used to. I avoided skipping dialogue through my playthrough to get the whole experience. Either way, even when I felt it dragged a bit, it was still interesting. I still got the feels. 

 Some areas graphically look weird, like on islands trees are cut into nothing on the boarders of the walkable area, which looks a bit strange, and a few story choices seemed slightly weird to me, but there is a chance I missed something, and they all really can be overlooked. 

That's the long and short of what I've got to say. I'm very intrigued, and will follow this developer and whatever they create in the future. This was good, but I want more, like stopping before that last gulp of water at 2am that would really satiate your thirst. Do get this game, its cheap, look stunning and is overall pretty interesting in general. I cannot wait to see what comes next, and will be eagerly awaiting!
